# 1 Enoch Chapter 95 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**1** Would that my eyes were a cloud of waters, that I might weep over you and pour out my tears like a cloud of waters, so that I might have rest from my anguish of heart!

**2** Who permitted you to practice reproaches and wickedness? So judgment shall overtake you, sinners.

**3** Fear not the sinners, you righteous; for the Lord will again deliver them into your hands so that you may execute judgment upon them according to your desire.

**4** Woe to you who pronounce anathemas that cannot be reversed — therefore healing shall be far from you on account of your sins.

**5** Woe to you who repay your neighbor with evil, for you shall be repaid according to your works.

**6** Woe to you, lying witnesses, and to those who weigh out injustice, for you shall suddenly perish.

**7** Woe to you, sinners, for you persecute the righteous; you shall be delivered up and persecuted in turn because of injustice, and heavy shall its yoke be upon you.

---

*LOGOS notes: The lament of vv. 1–2 is unusual in the woe oracle cycle — the author's personal grief at the wickedness he must condemn. V. 3 provides a brief word of reassurance to the righteous before the next series of woes. V. 4 targets those who invoke irrevocable curses (a priestly or judicial abuse). V. 6 targets false witnesses in legal proceedings. The lex talionis principle (v. 5) underpins the eschatological justice of the entire Epistle.*
